module_title: Patterns of Coercive Control in Parenting
learning_outcomes: Understand coercive control as a pattern of parenting behaviours.
Identify early signs of domination, fear-based compliance, and emotional destabilisation.
Recognise developmental impacts on attachment, self-regulation, and wellbeing.
Apply safe, supportive, developmentally appropriate alternatives.
Demonstrate mastery through quizzes, tasks, and scenario-based assessments.

lesson_content.definition: Coercive control in parenting is a pattern of behaviours that restrict a child’s autonomy, emotional safety, and ability to develop independence.

patterns.name: Invasion of Autonomy
examples: Interfering with privacy, sleep, or personal space

patterns.name: Isolation from Support
examples: Preventing contact with friends or extended family
Creating dependency for approval or information

patterns.name: Threats and Intimidation
examples: Using silence or withdrawal to create fear

patterns.name: Economic and Resource Control
examples: Restricting access to food, clothing, hygiene items

video_lesson.title: Coercive Control in Parenting: Understanding Patterns That Harm Children
script: In parenting, safety and connection form the foundation of healthy development.
Coercive control is not discipline—it is domination.
These patterns teach children to comply out of fear rather than trust.
Understanding these patterns helps parents build safer, healthier relationships.

activities.description: Sort behaviours into correct coercive control pattern categories.
Identify pattern, impact, and safer alternative.

scenarios.text: Parent alternates between affection and sudden withdrawal.
